Subject: GPU floorplan validation & provisional hold request — VendettaAI late-stage

Hi Jordan / Neha,

VendettaAI went green during execs last night and sales asks we validate a short-term node plan to support their Q1 POC and early-prod ramp. They want a provisional allocation while we finalize legal/PO (expected by 11/05). Key asks from their side:

- Target steady-state throughput: ~180 qps (text-gen, 2048 context)
- Peak bursts up to 600 concurrent infer requests for short windows
- Preferred instance flavor: equivalent to 8xA100-80GB (they'll mix quantized and fp16 models)
- Initial committed runway: 12 weeks, with option to ramp to dedicated pool after PO

Can Ops confirm current availability across us-west and whether we can place a soft hold for ~24 effective A100-80GB equivalents starting 2026-11-01 through 2027-01-31 (soft expiration if PO missing)? Folklore from previous cycles says we should size some buffer for batching and KV cache pressure — suggest adding 10% headroom unless Ops advises otherwise.

I've attached the Vendetta capacity request sheet with their projected token QPS and model footprints. Jordan — if you agree, can you escalate for commercial signoff and legal timeline? Neha — can you give an ops feasibility estimate and a provisional hold id if we can accommodate?

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Marcus — thanks for moving quickly.

Confirmation from our side: the POC workload will run the following models concurrently:
- gen-v3-main (fp16) ~ 60% of traffic
- reranker-v2 (int8) during peak windows

We modeled this as ~24 equivalent A100-80GB nodes for baseline with short bursts up to 40 nodes for spikes. 24 nodes fits their latency and token budget at expected QPS. If Redwood can provide a hold id and an expiration (we understand max 6 weeks without PO), we will prioritize getting the PO signed and aim to convert to a dedicated SKU and 12-month commit.

Let me know if you need anything else from procurement — I can push the internal PO tracker.

Jordan / Marcus —

We ran the floorplan with the supplied sheet and current node inventory. Summary below:

- Baseline requested: 24 A100-80GB equivalents -> Mapped to SKU: redwood.gpu.prod.a100e.8 (equivalent packing: 3 physical nodes per SKU due to pod sizing)
- Burst headroom to 40 nodes -> Achievable via autoscale across redwood.gpu.burst.* pool (will require cross-AZ balancing)
- Proposed operational buffer: +10% (as Marcus suggested) -> final baseline allocation = 26 A100-equivalents; burst cap = 44
- Us-west availability window: capacity exists but requires borrowing 8 nodes from reserved test pool for the 11/01 — 11/21 window. That pool is idle for a short period; ops approves one-time temporary reassign with the following constraints.

Provisional hold details:
- Hold ID: HOLD-6729-PROV
- Hold window: 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z through 2026-11-21T23:59:59Z (21 days)
- Auto-release: 2026-11-22T00:00:00Z unless PO/commit received and conversion ticket is created
- Billing exposure: no charges while marked soft-hold (we require signed PO to bill and move to Reserved). If PO misses conversion, ops will release without charge but capacity may not be available afterward.

Attachments: hold_terms_v1.pdf (term summary), vendetta_capacity_request_2026-10-20.xlsx (annotated by Ops).

Notes / action items:
- Jordan: flag commercial/legal to deliver PO by 2026-11-18 to allow conversion before auto-release.
- Marcus: coordinate with Elena to confirm PO timeline and accept the 21-day provisional window.
- Ops: will create conversion ticket once PO uploaded to our portal; otherwise HOLD-6729-PROV will lapse.

If we need longer than 21 days, Ops will consider extension but requires approval from Capacity leadership and a nominal pre-bill retention fee.

Neha Kapoor
Capacity Planning Manager
Redwood Inference
